# Refusal inventory — wave-24-fixit-1811 (T13, D10, AC-6.6)

Every refusal site in `payload/scripts/lib/walls.sh`, `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh`,
`hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh` and `hooks/stop-guard.sh`, with the fix line it prints or the
reason no line exists. `tests/refuse.test.sh` §INV reads each file's call sites (a
`fold_block`, `refuse`, `dp_finding`, `budget_deny` or `deny` call at the start of a statement)
and keys each site by where it is: `<file>:<function>`, the innermost shell function whose body
holds the call, or `<file>:(main)` for the file's top level (wave-36 T6; D12, AC-6.2). Each key
must appear here inside a bullet that carries `— fix:` or `— none:`, once per site the function
holds. So a reworded refusal needs no edit here, and a call moved into another function does.
The quoted text after a key is the refusal's fact when the call spells one, a reader's aid that
no check reads. A `<root>` or `<hooks>` in a fix below is the real plugin root or hooks
directory in the printed line; the placeholders here only stand for it.

- `payload/scripts/lib/walls.sh:wall_protect_main` — "main is a protected branch here" — protect-main, push to main — none: the push belongs to the human at their own terminal; no line the agent could paste is the fix
- `payload/scripts/lib/walls.sh:wall_protect_main` — "this is a force push" — protect-main, force push — none: the same, a force push is the human's own act
- `payload/scripts/lib/walls.sh:wall_protect_main` — "the current branch is protected" — protect-main, commit on a protected branch — none: the fix is a branch whose name is the reader's choice (`git switch -c <branch>` would print a placeholder)

- `payload/scripts/lib/walls.sh:wall_background_suite_guard` — budget arm, the full tree — fix: `tests/run.sh --only <first budgeted suite>`, the one door (wave-28 T36; it was `bash tests/<first budgeted suite>`, which the door now refuses)
- `payload/scripts/lib/walls.sh:wall_background_suite_guard` — " " — the one door: a dispatched agent's bare suite run, in any form the classifier reads, in a project whose tests/run.sh takes `--only` (wave-28 T36, REQ-10's door; D27, AC-10.1; T54 gave it the condition: with no runner, or one without `--only`, the run goes on to the budget) — fix: `tests/run.sh --only <suite>`, the refused suite's file name in place of `<suite>` when it is a plain name and fits the line
- `payload/scripts/lib/walls.sh:budget_unrecorded` — "no suite set is recorded for this agent" — budget arm, no suite set recorded for the agent — fix: `bash <root>/hooks/session-poker.sh amend <name> --suites+ <suite> --reason '<why>'` (`--reexec+ '<cmd>'` for a run; `_budget_remedy_line`) when a roster row carries the agent, and `amend <agent id> …` when none does: amend records a set for an agent its start did not place (wave-27 T38), and the detail says why it was not placed when its type is not a bionic: role
- `payload/scripts/lib/walls.sh:wall_memory_store` — "this writes the memory store" — memory wall — none: the fix is to write record/<wave>/assumptions.md or a rule proposal instead, content only the writer has

## payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh

- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_landing_gate` — "this branch touched undeclared files" — landing sweep, undeclared files — fix: `bash <root>/hooks/session-poker.sh amend '<name>' --files+ '<path>'… --reason '…'` per row (`LG_FIX`); revert is the other way out and has no single command
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_landing_gate` — "a dispatched agent's contract is unmet" — landing sweep, unmet contract — none: the fix is the named artifacts themselves, which only the agent can write
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_patrol_duties` — "the bound plan cannot be read" — stop, bound plan unreadable — fix: `chmod u+r` on the plan, named in the detail
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_patrol_duties` — "a cron was created with no CronList first" — stop, cron created without CronList — none: the fix is the CronList and CronDelete tool calls, not a shell command
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_patrol_duties` — "a FILL and a STANDDOWN went unanswered" — patrol duties, fill and stand-down — fix: `bash <hooks>/session-poker.sh hold NAME 'why it stays up'`, one per stood-down name in NAME, for the stand-down half; the fill half is an Agent dispatch or `bash <hooks>/session-poker.sh decline IDS 'why they wait'`, the named rows comma-joined in IDS (wave-27 T34)
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_patrol_duties` — " " — patrol duties, fill alone — fix: an Agent dispatch of the named rows, or `bash <hooks>/session-poker.sh decline IDS 'why they wait'`, the named rows comma-joined in IDS (FILL_REASON; wave-27 T34)
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_patrol_duties` — "a STANDDOWN went unanswered" — patrol duties, stand-down — fix: `bash <hooks>/session-poker.sh hold NAME 'why it stays up'`, one per stood-down name in NAME (STANDDOWN_REASON)
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_patrol_duties` — "a launch is not recorded in the plan" — patrol duties, a launch the plan lacks — fix: the task-set and ledger-add commands that `session-poker.sh launch-sync` prints (LAUNCH_REASON)
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_patrol_duties` — "a Patrol marker turn ran no tick" — patrol duties, marker turn ran no tick — fix: `bash <hooks>/session-poker.sh tick` (NOTICK_REASON)
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_patrol_revive` — "the Patrol fires but never ticks" — patrol revive, fires but never ticks — fix: `bash <hooks>/session-poker.sh tick`, and the job replaced with `session-poker.sh prompt`'s text
- `payload/scripts/lib/stop.sh:stop_patrol_revive` — "the Patrol died mid-run and nothing said so" — patrol revive, Patrol died — fix: CronList, CronCreate, then `bash <hooks>/session-poker.sh arm` (or `disarm`)

- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:dp_brief_sink` — " " — brief.sh sink forwarder — none: a forwarder; brief.sh findings carry their own fix (the impact timeout names Suites:/Files:)
- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:(main)` — "head ${_fr_short} is already proved" — full run on the proved head — none: the head is proved and there is nothing to run; the detail names the proof line and its evidence
- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:(main)` — "rows write tracked files: ${_fr_ids}" — full run while rows write the head — none: the fix is landing or dropping those rows, acts not commands
- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:(main)` — "the plan declares regression: no" — full run on a plan that declared `regression: no` at Step 0 (wave-31 T27, T26; rule 1) — fix: `bash <hooks>/session-poker.sh regression yes '<the reply, verbatim>'`, put to the user first; printed whole in the detail
- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:(main)` — "a second whole run on this plan" — a second whole run after one was launched (wave-31 T26; rule 5) — fix: dispatch the fix row's suites; for a second whole run, a verify row that reads `approval:regression-2, head`, and on the user's reply `bash <hooks>/session-poker.sh approve regression-2 '<the reply, verbatim>'`, printed whole in the detail
- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:(main)` — "row ${DP_BOUND_ROW} has a live writer ${DP_LIVE_WRITER} (session ${DP_LIVE_SID:0:8})" — a dispatch that re-marks a row whose writer is still open on a roster, this session's or another's, which would put two writers in one tree (wave-35 T7; REQ-5; T28 read every session's roster and named the session, T31 brought this line up to date) — fix: land the finished writer and the Patrol's ack closes the row, or `bash <hooks>/stop-orders.sh stopped <name>` for a writer that was stopped (it writes the ack); the detail names the row, the writer and the tree
- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:dp_deadline_hit` — "the wall ran out of time" — the dispatch wall's own deadline, 3 s under the hook's 15 s registration: the wall had not finished and refuses first, since the harness cancels a hook at its timeout and admits the call (wave-28 T70; A-orch-205 to 212, A-orch-231) — fix: `dispatch again`; the detail names the roster the row would have gone to and says nothing was spawned
- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:(main)` — "the roster path is a symbolic link" — the session's roster path is a symbolic link, so nothing is written through it and the launch is refused instead of admitted silently (wave-28 T70) — fix: `remove the link`, printed in the detail as `rm <roster>`
- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:(main)` — "the launch row did not build" — `roster_row` refused a field of the launch, so there is no row to append and the dispatch is refused instead of journalled blank (wave-28 T70) — fix: `/bionic:doctor`, and a reinstall when it reports nothing
- `hooks/dispatch-preflight.sh:(main)` — "the roster cannot be written" — the append to the roster failed (an unwritable state directory or file), so the dispatch is refused instead of warned about and admitted (wave-28 T70) — fix: `make it writable`; the detail names the roster path and the shell's own reason

## hooks/stop-guard.sh

- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:deny` — " " — stop-guard deny() forwarder — fix: `${OBSERVE_CMD} <target>` (`bash <hooks>/stop-check.sh <target>`), printed runnable
- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:(main)` — " ] || deny " — stop names no target — fix: the observe command, through deny()
- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:(main)` — "this stop carries no transcript path" — no transcript path — fix: `/bionic:doctor`
- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:(main)` — "the state directory is a symlink" — state directory is a symlink — none: which symlink to remove and why is the human's judgment; the detail names the path
- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:(main)` — "this target is on no roster row of this session" — target on no roster row — fix: the observe command, through deny()
- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:(main)` — "that name has more than one live row" — name with several live rows — fix: the observe command with the full id, through deny()
- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:(main)` — "that alias is not accepted for this agent" — alias not accepted — fix: the observe command with the agent's own name, through deny()
- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:(main)` — "the session roster carries no id for it" — no agent id on the roster — fix: the observe command, through deny(); or the human's own stop
- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:sg_deadline_hit` — "the stop guard did not finish in ${SG_DEADLINE_S} s" — the stop guard's own deadline, 3 s under the hook's 10 s registration: a stop the guard cannot judge is refused, not admitted; a recorded human order is read first and is never refused by it (wave-28 T70; A-orch-231 3) — fix: `stop again`, with the human-order route in the detail
- `hooks/stop-guard.sh:(main)` — "the stop could not be recorded" — the orchestrator's recorded stop of an unrostered agent could not be written onto the roster as its closed row, so the stop is not made (wave-28 T70) — fix: `make the roster writable`; the detail names the roster
